summary: This bill creates a new Social Security office to pay $250 per month (adjusted for inflation) to qualifying US adults ages 19-67 and funds it with a new 2.5% tax on adjusted gross income above $60,000 for joint filers.

scores.thoughts: The bill establishes a new universal adult assistance program that pays $250 per month (with inflation adjustments) to every qualifying adult aged 19-67 who applies. This creates a large-scale, ongoing federal spending obligation administered through a new Office of Universal Adult Assistance within the SSA. The legislation is therefore primarily about expanding government outlays.

Section 3 creates a new 2.5% supplemental tax on adjusted gross income above an exemption threshold ($60,000 joint / $30,000 single, inflation-adjusted). This is an explicit tax increase on individuals and is presented as the funding mechanism for the new payments. The bill therefore directly raises taxes.
